_note: Scenarios and labels written by the project author. 'borderline' means reasonable lawyers could disagree. Tune on split=dev, run split=test once at the end.

scenarios.text: A city deploys a system that scores residents' trustworthiness from their social media posts and shopping habits and uses the score to limit access to public housing.
A toy uses hidden audio cues below children's awareness to push them to keep playing and spend money.
A call-centre app analyses employees' voices to infer their emotions during shifts and flags 'unhappy' staff for disciplinary review.
A company builds a face-recognition database by scraping photos from social media and CCTV footage without consent.
A police tool predicts whether a named individual will commit a crime solely from their personality profile and neighbourhood.
A school platform infers students' emotional states from webcam video during lessons to grade their engagement.
A system categorises people from facial images to infer their sexual orientation or political opinions.
Live facial recognition cameras in a train station let police identify passers-by in real time against a watch list.
A recruitment tool ranks CVs and filters out candidates before a human recruiter sees them.
A bank uses a model to decide whether consumers get a loan and to compute their credit score.
A university uses AI to decide which applicants are admitted.
An AI system watches students through their webcams during online exams to detect cheating.
A hospital uses AI to triage patients arriving at its emergency department.
A life insurer uses an algorithm to set premiums from applicants' health data.
A platform allocates tasks to gig workers and evaluates their performance from behaviour data.
AI software that is a component of a medical device and diagnoses skin cancer from images.
A system that controls the safety functions of a regional electricity grid.
A border authority tool assesses the security risk of travellers entering the country.
An assistant for judges that researches case law and suggests how the law applies to the facts of a case.
A public agency uses AI to decide whether people are eligible for housing benefits.
An emotion recognition system in a shop infers customers' moods to decide which adverts to show.
A system decides which users are shown which job adverts, targeting adverts to selected groups.
A tool profiles job applicants to predict their personality and ranks them; a recruiter only does a quick formality check of the ranking.
A lie-detection tool that police use during interviews of suspects.
Authorities use AI to examine and assess asylum applications.
A customer-service chatbot on a retail website answers questions about shipping.
A tool generates realistic images of people for marketing, and the images are published online.
A video app lets users swap faces to create realistic fake celebrity clips and publish them.
A news site publishes AI-written articles about local politics with no human editorial review.
A voice assistant answers customers' phone calls and never tells them it is a machine.
A spam filter for a company's email.
An AI opponent in a video game that adapts to the player's style.
A warehouse tool that optimises shelf stocking from sales history.
A grammar-checking plug-in for a word processor.
A recommendation engine that suggests films to users of a streaming service.
A predictive-maintenance model for factory machines that is not a safety component.
A tool that only sorts incoming job applications into folders by role for a recruiter, without scoring or ranking candidates.
A system that flags inconsistencies in an examiner's already-completed grading so the examiner can review them.
An AI system developed and used exclusively for military targeting.
A university lab trains a prototype classifier solely for scientific research and never deploys it.
A hobbyist uses a photo-sorting AI for their own personal family albums.
